evidence: createApp registers Express routes and passes each operation to services.orders.* and services.inventory.*; it contains no business logic of its own
POST /orders handler only checks the request's shape and types (isRecord, typeof checks) and then calls services.orders.placeOrder
toErrorResponse maps domain error classes to HTTP status codes (409, 404, 400, 500); this is a transport concern
parseStateQuery and the /transitions handler rely on the domain's isOrderState/ORDER_STATES rather than repeating the state rules
No business rules here (e.g. quantity > 0, stock checks, transition rules); those are left to the application and domain layers
parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/infrastructure/http.ts is an HTTP transport adapter, and everything it does fits the infrastructure layer. It sets up the Express app and its routes and parses request bodies, path parameters and query strings into typed values. It maps domain and application errors to HTTP status codes and response bodies. Every business operation (placing orders, changing state, advancing, cancelling, reading stock) is handed to the application services. The input checks only confirm that values have the right type and are present (for example, that customerId is a non-empty string and quantity is a number). They do not enforce business rules such as positive quantities, stock availability or which state transitions are allowed. Checking whether a state value is valid is done by calling the domain's own isOrderState and ORDER_STATES, not by copying that logic into this file. Turning errors into HTTP responses is a transport concern. No persistence or business logic is mixed into this adapter.
